To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical strain rate at the GBS to DC transition, the stress exponent in the flow stress, the flow stress in the GBS and DC regimes, and the deformation mechanisms are all sensitive to the fraction of freely-sliding grains.

the critical strain rate at the transition from grain boundary sliding to dislocation creep varies from 10 3 to 10 5 as the fraction of freely-sliding boundaries is increased from 0% (no grain boundary sliding) to 100% all sliding boundaries are free to move.

the fraction of freely-sliding boundaries f in a microstructure is the most important factor in determining the creep response of AA5083 at 450 deg. C and that the transition between GBS and DC occurs at lower strain rates for microstructures with lower values of f.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the effects of grain boundary heterogeneity on the creep behavior of polycrystalline materials.
the influence of heterogeneities on the constitutive response of polycrystalline materials. In particular
the influence of heterogeneities in the microstructure of a material on its macroscopic behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the flow stress and deformation mechanisms are determined by the average grain boundary sliding resistance, and are insensitive to the detailed spatial arrangement of the sliding resistance.

grain boundary sliding resistance heterogeneity is important and must be taken into account in order to understand and model the creep behavior of polycrystalline materials, but that the detailed nature of that heterogeneity is not important.
the constitutive behavior is sensitive to the fraction of freely-sliding boundaries, but is not sensitive to the spatial distribution of sliding boundaries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the deformation mechanism transition from grain boundary sliding (creep rate < 10 -4 s 1) to dislocation creep (creep rate 10 -4 to 10 2 s 1) is determined by the fraction f of freely sliding boundaries.
grain boundary sliding resistance is a key parameter in the deformation of aluminum at high temperatures.
the constitutive behavior and deformation mechanisms of AA5083 are sensitive to the fraction of freely slipping boundaries in a polycrysal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the deformation behavior of a polycrystalline aggregate depends strongly on the fraction of freely-sliding boundaries, but is not very sensitive to the spatial distribution of sliding resistances.
heterogeneity of sliding resistance in a polycrytal can have a dramatic effect on the creep response, and the deformation mechanisms.
grain boundary sliding resistance can strongly affect the deformation mechanism and flow stress of a polycrystalline aggregate.
